subject: business-studies
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Flow production is most suitable for:
options: Mass-producing large quantities of identical, standardised products
questions.explain: Flow (mass) production continuously makes large quantities of identical products, e.g. cars or canned drinks.

options: Output produced per unit of input (e.g. per worker) in a given time
The total amount of stock held
questions.explain: Productivity measures output per input, such as the number of units produced per worker per hour.

questions.q: What is the difference between quality control and quality assurance?
options: Quality control checks products at the end; quality assurance builds quality into the whole process
Quality control happens only after sale
questions.explain: Quality control inspects finished goods, while quality assurance builds quality in at every stage.

questions.q: What does Just In Time (JIT) stock management aim to do?
options: Keep stock levels to a minimum, with materials arriving as needed
Hold very large stocks at all times
questions.explain: JIT keeps stock to a minimum, with supplies arriving just as they are needed, reducing storage costs.

questions.q: Which is a benefit of using technology such as automation in operations?
options: It removes the need for any quality control
It can increase productivity and consistency
questions.explain: Automation can raise productivity and produce more consistent output, though it has set-up costs.

questions.q: Job production is best described as:
options: Making products in groups or sets
Making identical products on a continuous line
Producing one-off, customised products to a specific order
questions.explain: Job production makes single, often customised items, such as a tailored suit or a bridge.

questions.q: What does TQM (Total Quality Management) involve?
options: Every employee taking responsibility for quality
Only the quality team checking products
Checking quality only at the end of production
questions.explain: TQM is an approach where everyone in the business is responsible for maintaining quality.

options: Making groups of similar products together before switching to another batch
questions.explain: Batch production makes a quantity of one product, then switches to make a batch of another, e.g. bread.

options: Always producing the cheapest possible product
Producing output using the fewest resources and least waste
Hiring as many workers as possible
questions.explain: Efficiency means getting the most output from the available inputs while minimising waste.

questions.q: What is a drawback of holding too much stock (overstocking)?
options: Money tied up in stock and higher storage and waste costs
questions.explain: Holding excess stock ties up cash and increases storage, insurance and potential wastage costs.

options: Sourcing and buying the materials and supplies a business needs
questions.explain: Procurement is the process of finding suppliers and purchasing the inputs a business needs.

options: A fall in average cost per unit as output increases
A rise in average cost per unit as output increases
questions.explain: Economies of scale mean the average cost per unit falls as a business produces on a larger scale.
